At times, your determination will be tested by self-questioning and despair, but it is precisely at these moments that you must do everything in your power to avoid being "depressed about being depressed!" The ideas below are good examples to follow. Name your beast. Winston Churchill referred to his depression as his "black dog." By personifying it as a small companion, you make this difficult situation more manageable. By naming it, you transform it into a state, rather than something that defines you. You might say something like, "My black dog is making me irritable today," instead of saying, "I am always irritable; it’s hopeless." Find a role model. Do you think you are the only one experiencing depression? Go to the library and browse through five biographies. You will likely find that at least one was written by someone who has suffered from depression. Do some online research to find famous people who have gone through depression. Look at how many celebrities have revealed the battle they fight against depression. Read their stories and note that others have managed to overcome their depression, and now you can draw inspiration from their experiences! Be gentle with yourself. Life is neither a race nor a competition. As a person, you matter and you have great value. Making things harder for yourself only results in self-attack. Avoid obsessing over your depression or making it something sacred to hide behind when things seem too difficult. The feedback loop created when you are angry at yourself for being depressed will only amplify that despair. Try again to name your struggle and distinguish it from who you are. Accept that the journey to well-being consists of small steps. Make a list of things that bother you outside of your depression. These could be unpaid bills, a need for a vacation, or a difficult job. In another column, write down practical things you think you can do to address what bothers you. For example, you could find ways to pay those bills, plan a vacation, or look for a new job. This is a vital aspect of overcoming depression. To progress, it is crucial to combat negative thought patterns. Cognitive-behavioral therapy and other forms of psychotherapy are helpful when you want to unlearn negative thinking and establish thought patterns that promote your self-esteem and increase your confidence. It is best to confide in a qualified person who can guide you in changing your way of thinking, but there are still some important points to keep in mind. Recognize that this feeling will pass. This step may be challenging, but it is essential as it helps you dispel your feelings of despair. Make a list of all your strengths. When you are depressed, you tend to downplay the positive thoughts you might have about yourself. Instead, list everything that is good about you. Don’t forget your past successes and your hopes for the future, even if they seem random. If you can’t write this list, ask a trusted friend or family member to do it for you. You can update this list as you work through your depression. Self-acceptance is absolutely essential to getting out of depression, as it makes you aware that there are positive things in you, but also that you have challenges to face. This will help you stop judging yourself more harshly than anyone else. Make decisions, even small ones, and follow them with actions. This is something that is very difficult to do when you are depressed, but it is essential to combat the feeling of helplessness that afflicts depressed individuals. Small decisions like getting out of bed, calling friends, or cleaning the kitchen will do the trick. Once you act on them, they become successes. Learn to replace negative thoughts by focusing on them. Am I imagining the worst? Am I condemning myself for something bad that happened? Am I focusing on my weaknesses instead of my strengths? It would be helpful to organize negative thoughts in one column and write rationalized thoughts in another column, so you can confront and dismantle the former. In one column, you might write the thought: "I am a failure," and in the second, you could challenge that thought with: "I made a mistake. I have made mistakes in the past and everything turned out fine. I have also had many successes." Once you have challenged the hardest aspects of your negative thoughts, learn affirmation techniques. Affirmation techniques will allow you to find a way to stand tall without succumbing to feelings of anger, fear, or helplessness. It is important to be assertive to avoid falling back into depressive tendencies in the future. Sit down and try to identify what is good in your life. Whatever they are, these good things deserve to be found. Regularly revisit this list and update it. In your initial list, there might be one or two things like "my home" or "my spouse." Over time, the list will grow as you begin to see joyful things in your life again. Replace sad thoughts with happy memories. You can control what you think about. Choose positive and happy memories over sad thoughts. Change your language to begin viewing things more positively. By saying, "At least...," you transform something negative into something positive. You can also ask yourself, "What have I learned from this experience?" instead of regretting something and viewing it as a failure. Once you are affected by depression, you are vulnerable, and this condition is more likely to return to your life if you fail to manage its causes. Be aware of the warning signs, and respond constructively to take control of this issue before it truly starts. Aim to reduce its impacts and duration. In Quenya, the vowels are fixed, and their pronunciation does not change depending on their position in the word. The diacritic (the accent on the letter) indicates whether the vowel is short or long. Memorize the sounds of the vowels and practice pronouncing them. "Y" is not a vowel in Quenya; however, it is a vowel in Sindarin. Quenya is written with an alphabet called Tengwar. You speak Quenya but write in Tengwar. Most consonants in Quenya are pronounced similarly to those in French. There are some unique rules specific to Quenya, so learn and practice using them when you speak Elvish. The "c" in Quenya is always pronounced hard, like the "c" in "corbeau," and never like the "c" in "cerise." It is pronounced as a "k," which can be a bit confusing, as both letters appear in Tengwar but are pronounced the same way. All "r"s are rolled like in Spanish. The sounds "n," "ny," and "m" are always pronounced softly; they are called "nasal consonants" because they are pronounced by letting air pass through the nose. The letter "y" is always a consonant, pronounced with a harder sound like in "yo-yo." If the Quenya word begins with a vowel, accent the first syllable of the word, emphasizing it and pronouncing it distinctly. Let the other syllables roll off your tongue more softly. The stress patterns in Quenya are universal; if the word starts with "a," "e," "i," "o," or "u," accent the first syllable. When there are only two syllables, the accent always falls on the first, even if it does not start with a vowel. For example, a word like "umin" will be pronounced "OU-min" and not "ou-MIN." For words that do not start with a vowel and contain more than two syllables, always stress the third syllable. This means an Elvish word like "hyarmen" is pronounced "haram-EN," with the tone rising at the end. Many Middle Eastern languages have similar stress patterns, which might resemble Arabic or Aramaic initially. You may notice that there is always a vowel in the third syllable of every Quenya word. This is an almost universal pattern in Elvish, contributing to a more elegant pronunciation of these languages. Generally, you can manage to stress Elvish words even if you do not follow the language rules, by following the prosody rules of Italian when you speak Quenya. Native Italian speakers tend to use pronunciation patterns from their mother tongue to pronounce French words, which might give the impression of speaking Elvish correctly even if it's not accurate. For example, if you used an Italian accent, you would place the stress on the first syllable of words like "ando" and "vala," which is correct. In Tolkien's world, Quenya is spoken by the High Elves, scholars, and nobles. It is a sort of classical version of Elvish.

The "c" is always hard, pronounced like "k," and "r"s are rolled. Nasal consonants include "n," "ny," and "m," pronounced softly. Stress is placed on the first syllable if a word starts with a vowel, and on the third syllable for longer words. This results in a distinct and elegant pronunciation typical of Elvish, making it sound classical.

It is advised to transplant the cabbage outdoors about 2 to 3 weeks before the last frost. Check the long-term weather forecasts in your area to estimate this date. Once you know the expected date of the last frost, plan a date 2 to 3 weeks earlier to transplant the cabbages into the ground. For a fall harvest, transplant the seedlings 6 to 8 weeks before the average date of the first winter frost. Cabbages need several elements for good growth, including sunlight. When transplanting in the garden, look for an outdoor location that receives full sun for at least 6 hours a day. Avoid planting cabbages in the same bed as cauliflower, broccoli, tomatoes, or strawberries. Cabbages grow very well when planted next to cucumbers and beans. Cabbages require very fertile soil. Mix the soil from the bed where you want to plant them with an equal amount of well-decomposed compost or manure. Water the soil to keep it moist before transplanting the cabbages. The ideal pH for cabbages is between 6.5 and 7.5. You can test the acidity level of the soil in your garden with pH test strips, available in most garden centers or hardware stores. If you need to lower the soil's pH, incorporate more compost or manure to make it more acidic. If you need to raise its pH, incorporate powdered limestone. Plant the seedlings at the same depth as in the tray where you sowed the seeds (about 1 cm). Space them 30 to 60 cm apart and plant them in rows spaced about 60 cm apart. For the best possible results, transplant the cabbage seedlings on a cloudy day to avoid shocking them with sudden sun exposure. Lay a 2 or 3 cm layer of mulch on the soil surface. The mulch will retain moisture in the soil while the young plants grow, protect the cabbages from insects, and help maintain a consistent temperature in the soil. Shredded leaves, finely shredded bark, or compost are ideal for mulching cabbages. Cabbages need about 4 cm of water per week. If it does not rain enough, water the soil sufficiently to keep it moist throughout the growth of the cabbages. Continue to water the cabbages until they begin to mature. At that point, stop watering them to prevent the heads from splitting. Do this 3 weeks after transplanting them. When they start to produce new leaves and form a head, incorporate fertilizer into the soil. They need to be fertilized about 3 weeks after transplanting the seedlings by applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Fish emulsions, liquid fertilizers, bone meal, and cottonseed meal are good fertilizers for cabbages.

Examine your negative thoughts and worries by identifying the types of mental distortions associated with them, meaning you need to pinpoint the partial or false truths your mind is telling you. Here are some examples of cognitive distortions: 

- **Black-and-white thinking**: This type of thinking leaves no room for nuance. You are either good or bad, right or wrong; there is no complexity or middle ground.
- **Overgeneralization**: You take one negative experience and make it a blanket rule. This kind of thinking often includes words like "always," "never," or "everyone."
- **Mental filtering**: You filter out all the positive aspects of a situation, only focusing on the negatives. For instance, you may have had a great date but focus solely on the awkward moments in the conversation.
- **Jumping to conclusions**: You make negative conclusions without clear evidence, such as believing you know what others think or what will happen in the future.
- **Catastrophizing**: You fixate on the worst possible outcomes and exaggerate small problems.
- **Emotional reasoning**: You believe that what you feel at the moment is an objective reflection of reality. If you feel bad, it must mean the situation is bad.
- **Arbitrary rules**: You follow strict, often arbitrary rules and create unrealistic expectations about what should or should not be.
- **Labeling**: You label yourself and others based on perceived flaws, even if you have clear evidence to the contrary.
- **Personalization**: You take responsibility for situations beyond your control. For example, if it rains during a party you organized, you blame yourself for the bad weather.
- **Magnification and minimization**: You minimize your positive attributes while idealizing those of others. When someone compliments you, you refute it.

Create a "thought journal" for this purpose. When you have a negative thought, find a blank page and follow these steps:
1. Write down the trigger, which could be another thought, an event, or a situation, e.g., "I argued with my partner this morning before work."
2. Note the negative thought that came to you during and after the trigger. Ask yourself, "What was I thinking?" "What was I telling myself?" and "What was going on in my head at that moment?" You might have thought, "I messed everything up. This is the end of the relationship. He is tired of putting up with me; he doesn't love me anymore, and he will leave me."
3. Note the words that describe how you feel and underline those strongly linked to the trigger, e.g., "scared, alone, hurt." Underline "scared."
4. Review what you've written and try to identify unhelpful thought patterns, e.g., "catastrophizing, jumping to conclusions, black-and-white thinking."
5. Draw two columns under each negative thought: one for evidence supporting the negative thought and another for evidence against it. By filling in these columns, you can determine if your negative thought is based on something real.

Continuing with the argument example, the supporting evidence column might include: "He really got angry, turned red, and slammed the door. He didn't call me during his break like he usually does." In the counter-evidence column, you could write: "We've had worse arguments and always improved the situation by talking. He told me he needs a moment to calm down after getting angry, but when he’s calm, he becomes more rational and ready to compromise. Earlier this week, he said he has appointments all day today and won't be able to call me during his break. He has assured me multiple times that he is committed to making our marriage work, no matter what. We don't argue that often." This process allows you to view your thoughts objectively, analyze and evaluate them to see if they are based on facts rather than accepting them without question. Ask yourself the following questions about your negative thoughts and write the answers in your thought journal:
- What are different ways to view the situation?
- If I didn't have this kind of feeling about the situation, how would I see it?
- What are the realistic probabilities of this happening?
- How would an outsider see the situation?
- Is it really helpful for me to think this way?
- What are the things I tell myself that are actually useful?

If you experience no signs of reaction (such as redness or irritation), you can safely apply it to the rest of your face. Once you have installed Virtual DJ, open the software. You will first be asked to select a skin. Skins vary in complexity and give the program a different look. To start using Virtual DJ, choose the basic skin (default interface). Virtual DJ is a robust software that offers many possibilities, so you will need to familiarize yourself with it and explore its features. It is best to choose the clearest and easiest interface to manipulate. When you launch Virtual DJ for the first time, you will be prompted to select the folder containing your music. Choose the folders you want to add by navigating through your computer using the search bar, or on a Mac, using Finder. If you typically use iTunes, you can click on the iTunes music library file (iTunes.xml) found under My Music, iTunes Library. To begin, you must familiarize yourself with the three main areas of the program before you start playing your sound.

The active waveform. At the top of the screen (just above the decks), you can see a small rectangular window with waveforms (red and blue peaks and troughs) when you have loaded tracks. This window is dynamic, and the track scrolls from right to left inside, showing you the volume peaks. The small squares appearing under the waveform indicate the beats of the track that is or will be played. This way, you can visually follow the progression of the tracks and easily synchronize them when desired. This window is called the CBG (computer beat grid). When you perfectly align the red squares with the blue ones, the two tracks will be synchronized on the same beat (tempo). Load two tracks (one on the left deck and one on the right deck) by dragging them with your mouse from the directory on the left and have fun!

The decks. Called Decks, the virtual turntables represent physical turntables. Imagine you have two physical turntables in front of you. The right deck is red while the left one is blue, corresponding to the blue and red active waveforms you can see just above. The left virtual deck simulates a physical turntable, and when a track is played, a blue line (surrounding the deck) shows you the elapsed time and the time remaining before the end of the track. The right virtual deck is red and has the same functions as the left deck. Start a track, click on the deck playing it with the left mouse button, and move the mouse while holding the button down to listen to the result!

The mixer. The mixer placed between the two virtual decks allows you to make basic adjustments like changing the output volume, input (gain), bass, treble, and midrange, as well as balancing the sound more towards the right or left deck. Choose a folder containing tracks on the left side of the screen and click on it. You will see the tracks in that folder appear. You can select a track to play by dragging it with the mouse onto a deck or by clicking on the track title in the window under the mixer. Generally, the track will be added to the left deck, and the right deck is used for the next track. Click on the gear icon at the top right (settings). Here you can configure and customize Virtual DJ to suit your preferences for playback, mixing, and editing. Click on Settings and observe the available options. You will find options related to remote control, the internet, and skins. Click on Skins to access possible modifications. You can search online for new graphics and custom skins to change the appearance of Virtual DJ. Some skins are very nice, but others can sometimes make the software difficult to manipulate. You will find beautiful skins on the official Virtual DJ website. For Virtual DJ 7, click here, and for new skins for Virtual DJ 8, click here (right-click to open in a new tab). There are labels next to most of the software controls and buttons to make things easier and to make the software more user-friendly.

Play/pause. This button allows you to start a track and also to pause it. Stop. The function of this button is quite easy to guess, right? Beatlock. This feature allows you to lock the tempo of the track and synchronize other tracks to its beat. For example, if you want to scratch with the right (or left) deck, this function ensures that the track being played continues to scroll at the same speed. The beatlock function offered on Virtual DJ allows you to do things that are not possible with physical turntables. Pitch. This function allows you to temporarily or permanently change the tempo of a track. You have two ways to access it: using the two arrows next to the SYNC button (for a quick adjustment) or with the slider above these two arrows (for a permanent modification). This function allows you to perfectly synchronize one track with another in the middle of a mix. The keylock button above the slider allows you to change the speed of a track without changing its pitch. The Virtual DJ software has many users worldwide. Therefore, you will find many tips and valuable information online to learn how to use this program effectively. You will also find resources on YouTube and other websites.

Cricket requires specific and appropriate equipment to play properly. The minimum requirement includes six stumps (posts), four bails (wooden pieces that sit on top of the stumps), two cricket bats, and a ball. Most teams also wear appropriate uniforms and safety equipment for the wicketkeeper. The stumps and bails are wooden pieces assembled together to create what is called the wicket, one of the most important objects in cricket. The setup of the wickets is explained in detail at the end of this section.

The cricket bat is a large willow bat, flat on one side and rounded on the other to ensure its strength. The ball should be struck with the flat side of the bat for more power.

The cricket ball resembles a baseball in size and composition, but it is divided into two hemispheres stitched together, similar to a tennis ball. It is traditionally red, with a white seam. Nowadays, it can also be white for better visibility during important matches.

The cricket uniform consists of long trousers, a shirt (short or long-sleeved), and a pair of shoes. Most cricket players wear spikes for better traction on the field, although this is not mandatory. In matches with a traditional red ball, the uniform is generally white or cream, while colored uniforms are reserved for matches with a white ball.

The wicketkeeper (a ball catcher) can wear safety equipment similar to that of baseball catchers: a pair of gloves, leg pads, and a helmet. Other field players are not allowed to wear safety gear.

Cricket is played on a large oval-shaped field. At the center of the field is a rectangular area called the pitch. The boundaries of the field should be clearly marked by a line. The pitch is where the bowler delivers the ball to the batsman of the opposing team. The length of the pitch must be 20.12 meters with a width of 3.05 meters.

A cricket field is typically oval, although no specific shape is mandated by the rules of the game. The pitch is divided into several segments by lines called creases. There are four in total: The popping crease, sometimes called the batting crease, marks the limit from which the batsman is no longer safe and can be out (for example, when one of the wickets is broken by the opposing team during a run, this is called a run out).

The two return creases are parallel lines along the longest side of the pitch, located on each side from a popping crease to the end of the pitch. The white lines closing the pitch are called the bowling creases. They are parallel to the popping crease and are located between the two return creases, dividing the playing area into two rectangles on either side of the popping creases. The bowler may stand on or behind this line before delivering the ball. Each end of the pitch is marked by lines (creases), leaving a rectangular area between them at the center of the pitch. Outside these ground limits, the rest of the cricket field is unmarked. A wicket consists of a structure made of three wooden posts, called stumps, driven into the ground, with two small sticks called bails sitting on top of each pair of stumps (left-middle and middle-right). In most cases, if a bowler's ball hits a wicket and knocks off a bail, the batsman facing the delivery is out. Defending the wickets is therefore an important part of the offense. The three stumps must measure 71.1 cm in height (above the ground) and are spaced 22.86 cm apart.

The wickets are positioned so that the central stump is at the center of the bowling crease, and the other two stumps are equidistant from each other along the line. A wicket is placed in each bowling crease, totaling two wickets on the pitch. The batsmen stand in front of the wicket they are defending during the game.

Common conditions that often cause bloating include irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), celiac disease, and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. Other rarer conditions can also lead to bloating. Serious disorders that can cause bloating include ascites, tumors, celiac disease, dumping syndrome, ovarian cancer, and pancreatic insufficiency. For these conditions, your doctor may prescribe medications that will vary depending on the issue and its severity. Always follow your doctor's instructions regarding prescription medications. Your bloating should subside after 1 or 2 days with appropriate food or medical treatment. If it is not a serious case, it will eventually resolve on its own. However, some situations require medical attention. If your symptoms do not improve within 2 weeks following medical treatment, consult your doctor immediately. Do the same if you experience intense pain that prevents you from resuming daily activities or persists for days; you have acute diarrhea; you are vomiting; you see blood in your stool or notice a significant change in the frequency or color of your stool; you experience unexpected weight loss; or you feel chest pain.

Massage the injection area for about ten seconds to help the medication spread throughout your body. Even if the expiration date on your EpiPen has passed, you can still use it, though its effectiveness may be significantly reduced. ### Instruction 1:
Adopting a strategy to cope with rejection will help you avoid fearing it, as it allows you to build self-confidence in your ability to face it effectively. Instead of reflecting on the situation, we tend to react under the influence of our emotions and feelings. Your emotional state and physical health significantly affect your cognitive state, and you are likely to instinctively let your feelings and emotions take over. However, it is essential to remain calm and listen to what the person rejecting you has to say so that you can respond rationally and appropriately. For instance, how would you react to someone interrupting you in traffic while you were tired and sick, compared to someone interrupting you just after you learned you got a promotion? In the first case, you might be enraged, while in the second, you might let it go. The situation remains the same, but circumstantial factors, like your mood and physical state, influence your reactions differently. 

For another example, while you might want to yell at a recruiter for not hiring you, it is crucial to stay calm and respond appropriately in a professional setting. You do not have to appreciate their decision, but you should respond with respect. Keeping a journal can be very helpful for personal development and cognitive reflection, as it gives you a place to write down your doubts, fears, thoughts, ideas, and feelings. This way, you can better release them and avoid dwelling on things you cannot change (such as a breakup, a rejection letter from your university, or a scholarship application rejection). Writing can thus be a useful way to rid yourself of feelings of fear. The act of transforming your floating feelings and ideas into written phrases can help you understand them better. Regarding the fear of rejection, writing down such feelings can help you dominate them by evaluating them from a neutral and less emotional perspective.

Here are some examples of things you might note about rejection: the object of your fear of rejection (e.g., I fear being rejected by this person if I ask them out), how you will feel if rejected (e.g., worthless, unpleasant), the most likely reasons someone might reject you (e.g., because they recently broke up with someone), the positive aspects of rejection (e.g., I will have more time for myself and can seek new partners), what you might miss if you don’t try (e.g., if I didn’t make a move on this person, I would always wonder what it would have been like if I had). Have you ever thought something like, “if I don’t get into this school, it means I’m worthless and will never achieve anything?” or perhaps, “if this person rejected me, it means no one else will ever love or accept me?” These are examples of naive and black-and-white thinking. Such statements are incorrect generalizations from a single case to justify or explain your entire personality or nature. It is crucial to abandon such rigid thinking in favor of a deeper understanding of the meaning of rejection. Rigid and all-or-nothing thoughts are typically the results of strong emotional states like extreme sadness or anger. Being able to identify and master such feelings or thoughts will allow you to be resilient, stronger, and thus reduce your fear.

Here’s a process to follow: identify the all-or-nothing statements and write them down. For example, “if I don’t get this job, it means I’m worthless and will never achieve anything.” Identify all components of the all-or-nothing attitude. For example, “getting this job makes me useful, and not having it makes me useless.” Refute any fixed ideas. For example, “I didn’t have this job before, and my life has never been that useless.” Stay positive. For example, “I’ve applied for other jobs in the past and been hired. Now I have an excellent cover letter thanks to these jobs. I have very good interview skills.” Rejection is part of life, and one way to cope with your fear is to understand that it can happen, that it happens to many people, and that it does not mark an end, but in fact a new beginning. Have you applied for a job? Good, hundreds of people have too. Did you make a move on someone? There’s a 50% chance they’ll say no (and a 50% chance they’ll say yes!). Be aware that you can only control yourself, not anyone else. For example, if you apply for a scholarship, you won’t know what other candidates included in their resumes or applications. However, make sure you did your best. You can only control what you do, not what others do. Understanding that rejection is a normal thing will prepare you to face it effectively. You’ll see that it happens to everyone and that the world is not against you. Moreover, the more it happens, the more normal it becomes, and the less you will fear it. This may be easier said than done when you feel upset about your situation, but learning to accept it gracefully will benefit not only your mindset but may also be beneficial in the future.

Instead of lashing out, show understanding and empathy. On one side, you’ve probably already rejected someone in the past, and you know how it feels to break someone’s hopes. As the rejected person, here’s a situation where you’ll want to be the strongest without responding hurtfully or arrogantly. The more you can face it, the easier it will be to control the fear it evokes in you. For example, suppose you applied for a job you weren’t hired for. Most of us would stop there, but it may be more advantageous to go further by sending a letter to the recruiter thanking them for the time they took to review your application and respond. Such a note can help you close the chapter on that rejection and rid you of negative feelings. It is also vital not to burn bridges, as you may need to apply for another position at the same company someday. You might also accompany your thank-you note with a question like, “what aspect would you advise me to improve?” to know what the recruiter thinks would make you a better candidate in the future. For another example, if your crush rejects your advances, accept the rejection graciously by saying something like, “I understand and respect your decision. I hope we can always be friends.” You will appear as mature as respectful, which could earn anyone’s admiration. Although the person may not want to date you romantically, they might be happy that you left the possibility of friendship open.

Rejection happens, but you will not be rejected from everything. You will not be able to achieve your goals and dreams or even meet other people if you do not put yourself out there to create opportunities. Since you dared to try, it is normal to expect a bit of rejection sometimes. This is entirely normal because these opportunities were not necessarily meant for you, and it simply means that better opportunities await you. Remember that your life is not made up solely of rejection, and you still have more time ahead to experience success just as you do rejection. It is crucial to maintain a broader perspective that goes beyond the exact moment of your rejection situation. Look at your past and your future. If you find yourself overwhelmed by a particular situation in which you were rejected, ask yourself this question: “will this moment I am currently experiencing matter to me in a week, a month, or a year?” Being rejected by your crush may seem like the end of the world today, but a few days later, you might remember it as a minor incident. It may hurt you now, but with time, you will forget it and be able to move on. At 40, you will barely remember your crush, even though it is painful right now. Look to the past. Sure, you may not have landed that job you cared so much about. Yet, you have successfully applied to others. You know you can be hired because your resume proves it! One rejection should not dictate your entire life. Do not fear what has not yet happened. We often think there is a direct link between our feelings and the situation at hand. Note that rejection simply means you did not get something you were seeking. Feelings such as fear, doubt, sadness, and any other weakness are caused by yourself. Try to spot those moments when you assign intense feelings to neutral situations. For instance, suppose someone denies you a particular position. We sometimes react on impulse by thinking negatively like “he rejected me intending to hurt me.” However, what is more certain is that the person who rejected you was not even thinking about the rejection that deeply. For example, in the case of a job, the recruiter is much more focused on finding the ideal candidate than passing personal judgment on your abilities. They did not fail to hire you intending to hurt you, but because you do not seem to be the ideal candidate for the position. It is essential to make the effort to identify not only the objective meaning of rejection but also the feelings you assign to that reality. For example, “I was rejected for this position, which means I will never work for this company. This rejection provokes feelings of doubt about my skills. I feel sad because I felt very competent for this position.” Being able to identify the feelings you assign to the situation will help you become aware of your personal worries and doubts that you will examine in the next steps.

Maintain a broader perspective, recognizing that one rejection does not define your entire life. Accept rejection gracefully, and keep opportunities open for the future.

If you do not already know how to measure your waist (you may have needed it to buy pants, for example), it is very easy to do. Take a measuring tape and wrap it around your natural waist, which is usually located at the top of your hips, just below the navel. Look at the number where the tape overlaps: this is your waist measurement. Some women's belts are designed to be worn at the hips rather than at the waist. In this case, place the measuring tape a few centimeters lower so that it rests naturally at the top of your hips, then take the measurement as usual. The next step is to find fabric for your belt. If you do not have fabric on hand, you should be able to find some at a relatively low price in a craft store (or even online). Almost any type of comfortable and sturdy fabric is suitable for your belt. Whatever type of fabric you choose, you will need a strip measuring 17 or 18 cm longer than your waist measurement, with a width of 12 or 13 cm. Here are some fabrics that work well for belts: cotton (plain or patterned; cotton canvas is particularly durable), polyester, rayon, bamboo fabric, wool (it can be expensive). 

When your fabric is ready, lay it flat on your work surface lengthwise (so it goes from left to right) with the pattern facing down. Fold the long edges of the fabric over about 1.25 cm. Use a hot iron to press the folds well. Use thread and a needle or a sewing machine to sew the folded edges, leaving a seam allowance of about 75 mm. You need to do this so that none of the raw edges of the fabric are exposed once you finish your item. This is a golden rule in sewing: raw edges fray much faster than folded edges, so they should be avoided at all costs. Fold the ends of the fabric over about 1.25 cm and press them to mark the folds, as you did in the previous step. Then, fold the entire strip of fabric in half lengthwise to have a long, thin strip (with the pattern now visible). Press this fold, then sew along the bottom edge and the top edge (the one created by the fold you just made), leaving a seam allowance of about 75 mm. At this point, you are more or less finished. For this simple belt style, all you have to do is tie the belt around your waist and wear it. If you want, you can even add a decorative knot to personalize your belt even more! If the raw ends of your belt bother you, you can sew them just like you sewed the other edges of the fabric. Siphoning wine involves using a few relatively simple instruments, most of which are part of the basic equipment for anyone making wine at home or are available at any winemaking supply store. To siphon wine correctly, you will need: one or more sterilized carboys or buckets, a tube, and an airtight stopper for the wine. To sterilize your tube, you can use potassium metabisulfite or sodium metabisulfite diluted in water. You can find this type of solution commercially or mix it at home. Generally, one tablespoon of this solution should be diluted in about 4 liters of water. Everything that will touch the wine must be sterilized using the metabisulfite solution. Typically, you should pour a bit of the solution into the bucket or through the tube before disposing of it in a place where it won't cause problems. The metabisulfite solution is very harsh, so it is best to use it in a well-ventilated area while wearing a respirator mask and gloves when handling it. Follow the instructions on the package. Take the container with the wine and the sediment and open it, then place it on an elevated surface. Depending on how much wine you are going to produce, you may need a substantial surface area or just the surface of your table and the kitchen floor. Make sure your tube is long enough to reach the point from which you will siphon the wine. Siphoning relies on gravity, so it is essential that the barrel or tank filled with wine is positioned higher than the highest point of the clean bucket or carboy you will use to collect the wine; otherwise, it won't work. Place the cut end of the tube in the barrel, ensuring you do not touch the sediment at the bottom. It is better if you can see the sediment layer clearly at the time you are ready to siphon the wine, and it should be dark and thick enough. Let the tube go deep enough into the wine, but leave a space of at least 2 to 5 cm above the sediment layer. Insert the other end of the tube into the clean receptacle or let it hang above the receptacle. You will need to start siphoning before quickly inserting it into the receptacle. Make sure beforehand that the tube is long enough to reach the receptacle. It’s not very complicated: start sucking from the other end of the tube like you would with a straw until the wine begins to flow, then place the tube into the clean receptacle as quickly as possible. It takes a bit of practice to do this without ending up with a mouthful of wine or spitting it out. But hey, there are worse things in life than having a mouthful of wine... Once the wine starts to flow, quickly insert the tube into the receptacle and try to maintain a "steady" flow. Keep an eye on the sediment, ensuring it does not get resuspended or that neither of the tubes splashes and introduces too much oxygen into the wine. When the second receptacle is full or if the sediment begins to move, pinch the tube to stop the flow of wine and halt the siphoning. Making wine is as much an art as it is a science, and you will lose some wine during the operation. When have you siphoned enough wine? You will probably estimate this visually and make that decision for yourself. It's part of the job. Don’t complicate your life by trying to siphon just to the edge of the sediment layer. Just remove as much wine as possible and eliminate the sediment. If you are making wine yourself, there will always be a bit of sediment left at the end. Once you have transferred all the wine into the new container, install the airtight stopper, which you should screw tightly and lock. There are different types of airtight stoppers, each with its own instructions, so it is important to follow the manufacturer's instructions for your specific model. Most of them simply fit directly into the opening of the carboy.

Position the wine container higher than the receiving container. Maintain a steady flow and stop when the second container is full or sediment rises. Seal the wine with an airtight stopper according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

To draw a graph, you need two scales: one for the x-axis (abscissas), which often can be linear, and another for the y-axis (ordinates), which can be logarithmic or linear depending on the situation. Generally, the phenomenon is represented on the y-axis, but you can also place it on the x-axis for clarity. The curve will be the same in both cases, just oriented differently. The choice of scale depends on the data being represented and the type of analysis you plan to conduct. The x-axis usually represents the independent variable, which you control, like age groups in a study. An independent variable is not influenced by the phenomenon being studied and has a single relationship with it, such as a change over time. Examples of independent variables include specific dates (years, months, etc.), time spans, age groups, or increasing dosages of a medication. For extreme data that does not vary too much, use a linear scale (1, 2, 3… or 10, 20, 30…). For large gaps (e.g., between 4 and 1,000,000), use a logarithmic scale. Examples of exponential data include population explosions, rapid price inflation in a crisis, or compound interest investments. Examine your data closely to see if you must start from 0. If the lowest data point is in the millions and the highest in the billions, start your scale at 10^6. Subsequent increments would be 10^7, 10^8, and so forth. 

Once you have your pairs of data in the form (independent variable, dependent variable), plot the first point. Locate the first independent variable on the x-axis, such as a date or age. For beginners, it’s best to mark it lightly with a pencil, which can be erased later. Find the corresponding dependent variable on the y-axis for the provisional point you just plotted. If you’re using a decimal logarithmic scale, identify the two gradations between which your value falls, and place it on one of the ten intermediate gradations. For instance, between 10^6 (one million) and 10^7 (ten million), each fine line represents 1,000,000 units. Thus, the value 4,000,000 would be positioned between 1,000,000 and 10,000,000, specifically at the fourth small graduation above 10^6. With a logarithmic scale, 4,000,000 is in the upper half of the range, while it would be in the lower half (below 5,000,000) on a linear scale. The phenomenon of points clustering towards the upper end of the interval is consistent across the entire scale: this is the exponential effect. At the intersection of the two lines drawn from your points, place a dot. Proceed in the same manner with the other coordinate pairs, ensuring you do not confuse the gradations. When finished, simply connect the points in order, and your curve is complete.

After plotting all points, connect them to complete the graph.

Sometimes in a couple, one partner or even both may have doubts about the relationship. This person may tend to distance themselves, usually without providing an explanation to their partner. You might not know what’s wrong and wonder if you did something wrong. You might feel tempted to approach your girlfriend to determine what the problem is. However, this behavior may irritate the person who has doubts and push them to take action. If you find yourself in this situation, do your best to give her the space she needs. While this approach is not guaranteed to work, by stepping back for a few days or weeks, you might help your girlfriend realize that she values your relationship and feels lonely without you. Even if things don't go as you hoped, distancing yourself will also help you realize that you had a life before meeting your girlfriend, that you were happy, and that you can still live a fulfilling life without her. If you genuinely feel you cannot live without your girlfriend, you can take certain steps to try to save your relationship. However, it is important to understand that if your girlfriend is unhappy and does not want to be with you, both of you will be unhappy. Try to identify what aspect of your relationship makes her unhappy. The sad truth might be that she simply does not love you anymore. Other aspects could also be the root of her unhappiness. Try to identify these issues and work on resolving them. Surprise her. If you’ve been together for a long time, you might not be making much effort to keep her happy. Surprise her with something special, such as a candlelit dinner or taking her dancing at her favorite place. Even a small gesture, like bringing her favorite candies or flowers, can show her you’re thinking of her. Try to remind her of the good times. There is a reason you and your girlfriend got together, but during tough times, those reasons may seem distant. Try to revisit those reasons by recalling your first date or a shared laugh. You need to make her relive the positive feelings from the beginning of your relationship. Write her a love letter. This approach is simple, but many people love receiving love letters. It doesn’t mean you should be cheesy or overly sentimental; just write a straightforward letter reminding her how much she means to you. You could mention a fond memory you share or a common future project. Try to be more open and vulnerable. During this difficult time, you may be inclined to close off and share less with your girlfriend, which could worsen the situation. Instead, try to open up more to her. Share when you’re having a bad day, express your fears, and let her see this more vulnerable side of you. Encourage your partner to be independent. One reason your girlfriend may not be happy with you is that she feels smothered and unable to be independent. Encourage her to pursue her desires rather than doing everything to keep her by your side. For example, if she wants to apply to a prestigious school, offer to help with the admission process. If she wants to travel, encourage her to go for it. It may not be what you want, but sometimes the best solution is to let her go. If it is evident that she is unhappy with you but cannot leave for one reason or another, be brave and show her how much her happiness matters to you by deciding to break up with her yourself. You can do this gently by being honest. Tell her you realize she is no longer happy with you and that you know she doesn’t want to hurt you, but it’s time to end the relationship. This won’t necessarily make the breakup less painful, but at least you will have control over the situation. You may even feel relieved after being unhappy in your relationship for a while. When you end your relationship with your girlfriend, it’s important to let go of any anger you feel towards her. Dwelling on your anger and resentment will only make the situation harder. To move on, you will need time. If you feel sad after the breakup, know that you will feel better with time. You might adopt various strategies to feel better, but in any case, you need to give yourself time. There is no set duration for this process. You might need a few days, weeks, or even months. Try to see each passing day as a step in the right direction. The day after the breakup, you might be tempted to call your girlfriend or send her an email or text. However, this will only prolong your sorrow. If necessary, delete her number and remove her from all your social media. If she tries to contact you, ignore her call or message. If she sends you an email, delete it without reading it. This doesn’t mean you can never talk to her again; however, you will likely regret anything you might say immediately after the breakup, and it won’t do you any good. If you don’t want to completely get rid of her contact information, write it down and give it to a trusted friend, who will return it only when you are over the breakup. If you don’t want to get rid of certain items completely, such as by throwing them away or giving them away, put them in a box or bag and store them out of sight. If you fear being tempted to revisit memories with these items, either get rid of them completely or ask a friend to keep them for a while. While you have the right to spend an evening crying and feeling sad after the breakup, try to remain active. Make plans with friends and engage in things you enjoy. Participate in events where you can meet new people. If you have fun with people you love, you won’t have time to dwell on the loss of your girlfriend. Also, try to stay physically active. It is widely proven that being physically active helps with both mental and physical well-being. After the breakup, you may feel tempted to do nothing, but instead, try to go for a walk or run. If you enjoy team sports, join a club. While the end of a love story is always sad, you can still learn from it. Take the time to reflect on the relationship as honestly as possible. Your ex-girlfriend likely made many mistakes during your relationship, but you probably made just as many. Instead of dwelling on her faults, think about what you could have done better. For example, in your future relationships, you could work on better communication, so that your future girlfriends feel comfortable telling you when something bothers them. If in your last relationship you tended to get angry or defensive when your partner raised an issue, make an effort to be more open and calm when facing problems. It can be difficult to be honest with oneself about our own flaws. Keep in mind that hiding behind your pride won’t serve you well.

The visible sadness on your face can help your partner see that you genuinely care about their feelings, even as you end the relationship. If you think the conversation will last a while, try to have it when you won’t be interrupted by external factors. For example, don’t break up with your partner an hour before they go to work. Instead, visit them at home in the evening. This allows you to discuss all the issues. If you are gently breaking up with someone, you must take responsibility for your decision. Sometimes, people think it would be easier if their partner made the decision to break up. However, it is your feelings that have changed, and it is your responsibility to initiate the breakup conversation. If you try to lead your partner toward the breakup using hints, you will be dishonest and create a confusing situation. Your partner might not understand the message and may start questioning themselves as you subtly distance yourself. If you want to break up gently, you must take responsibility for your decision. It is important to be honest when ending a relationship. You are entitled to express this opinion. It will help your partner feel the end of the relationship because they will understand the logic. You can kindly say: "I’m sorry, but I don’t love you anymore. Now I need something different, and I think it’s best for us to go our separate ways." If the relationship was less serious, you can be more brief, for example: "I’m sorry, but I don’t feel anything special between us; I think it’s better if we stay friends." Honesty is important, but it shouldn’t be brutal. You shouldn’t dwell on your partner’s past mistakes or current issues. If you’re breaking up because you are no longer attracted to your partner, it’s best not to mention it. If you feel resentment due to past arguments, you might feel better expressing it, but it’s painful for your partner to hear. If you want to gently end a relationship, keep the reasons for the breakup general and avoid detailing your partner’s flaws. Again, while you should be honest, you also need to be direct. You’re not doing your partner any favors by beating around the bush and avoiding the subject. Start the conversation with a direct statement of what you want, for example: "I wanted to talk to you because I don’t feel this relationship is working." From there, keep the conversation brief. It can be hard to break up with someone, but it’s important to remain calm and composed. This way, you can express what you want concisely. Does the shape of your body resemble more of a pear, an apple, or an avocado? Everyone tends to gain weight as they age, and body shape, especially the waist-hip ratio, is a quick method to estimate fat distribution, which can indicate potential health risks such as high blood pressure, diabetes, heart attacks, and certain forms of cancer. To calculate this ratio, divide the waist circumference by the hip circumference. Ensure you measure your waist about 5 cm above the navel and your hips at the widest point. In this measurement, a ratio of more than 1.0 for men and more than 0.85 for women indicates that you have more belly fat than is healthy. Add one year if you exceed the recommended ratio. The Body Mass Index (BMI) is another way to measure your body status by dividing weight in kilograms by height in meters. A high BMI can indicate a significant amount of fat, which may expose you to obesity-related issues. To calculate it, simply multiply your height by itself (also known as squaring it) and then divide your weight in kilograms by your height squared. You now have your BMI. If you are above 25, you are overweight. For those not good at math, there are also websites that can do the calculation for you, such as this one. Add one year if your BMI is below 18.5 (underweight). Add two years if you are between 25 and 29.9 (overweight), and three if you are beyond 30 (obesity). Subtract one year if your BMI is between 18.5 and 25 (healthy weight). The most accurate way to assess your body composition, in addition to the waist-hip ratio and BMI, is to analyze your body fat percentage. The most accurate way to achieve this is through bioelectrical impedance. During this test, which you can do with a fitness trainer, you will lie down and place two electrodes on your foot. Then, a weak electrical current will be sent through your body. You will not feel this current. The test will then produce an accurate result of the proportion of fat and lean tissues like bones or muscles in your body for comparison with an average result. To obtain an exact result, you should not have exercised, used a sauna, or consumed alcohol in the hours preceding the test. Women also have more fat than men. For women, do nothing if the percentage is between 15 and 24%, and add half a year if it is between 25 and 33%. Add one year if you are below 15% or above 33%. For men, do nothing if the percentage is between 6 and 17%, and add half a year if it is between 18 and 24%. Add one year if you are below 6% or above 25%.

Before attempting your split, stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart. Lean forward onto your dominant foot (the one in front). It’s best to practice your splits on a soft surface, such as a classic or yoga mat. Avoid practicing on tile or hard floors if possible. Keep your front leg straight and gently slide forward, directly in front of you. Hold this position and do not let your body return to its original position or slide back. Try to take off your socks to prevent your feet from slipping. Another option is to do this exercise on a mat while keeping your socks on. As you stretch your front leg, do the same with your other leg, stretching it back while maintaining your position. When you feel a pull in your thigh, stop stretching your leg. Forcing your body to continue this exercise beyond that point can cause pain or injury. If necessary, use a small chair or table for balance as your body approaches the ground. When both legs are stretched as far as possible, take a pause and hold your position. Try to count to 15 or even 30. The goal is for your body to learn to relax while holding the stretch. Rest your arms on the small chair, table, or the ground if needed. Remember that stretching can create discomfort but should never cause pain. If you feel pain in this position, stop the exercise immediately. Once you have held your position as long as possible, gently return to your starting position. After resting for a moment, you can try the exercise again if you feel your body is ready. Take your time and focus on technique while practicing this exercise. Most people naturally lack flexibility. Mastering this exercise may take several months of practice. Be patient and don’t give up if you feel that your flexibility isn’t improving. Depending on your age, it may take longer.

There are two main types of tire swings: vertical and horizontal. The horizontal model has three attachment points to keep the tire horizontal, while the vertical model is attached at a single point. Both types are made in a similar way but with some minor differences. Generally, vertical swings are easier to install and require less time. It should have roughly the same characteristics needed to hang a traditional swing. Look for a sturdy hardwood tree, such as an oak, with a strong branch of the right size. The main difference from a traditional swing is that a tire swing needs to be placed further from the trunk of the tree, as this model swings much more side to side. Allow at least 1.5 m between the swing's attachment point and the trunk. If the branch is over 3 m high, you may need to leave even more distance. The main element of this swing is the tire. You can find inexpensive or even free tires at recycling locations, such as a dump or dealership. A completely worn-out tire is too dangerous for a car but perfect for a swing. Whether you plan to position the tire vertically or horizontally, you will need a cordless drill. To make a horizontal swing, take four chains of the same length, four stainless steel quick links, a swiveling safety hook, and three U-clamps. The chains should have a diameter of at least 1 cm and a length of 1 to 1.5 m. To make a horizontal swing, aside from the tire, you only need a strong rope. Since it is likely recycled, it may be very dirty. Even new tires can stain clothes and skin. Use a pressure washer to clean the tire before making it into a swing. If you don’t have a pressure washer, try using one at a car wash. When it rains, water needs to drain to prevent accumulation inside the tire, which could get you wet or dirty. Make a few holes in the part that will be closest to the ground. If you are making a horizontal swing, drill holes in the center of one of the side faces of the tire. If you are making a vertical swing, make one or two holes in the tread. Before installing the tire, ensure that it will be hung from a sturdy support. Attach the suspension rope or chain to the branch you have chosen. If you are making a horizontal swing, simply pass one of the four chains over the branch and attach both ends together using a quick link to form a closed loop. Hang the swiveling hook onto the quick link with the hook part facing down. To make a vertical swing, pass the rope over the branch and tie a slip knot (for example, a bowline) at one end. Pass the other end through the loop and pull so that the knot rises to the branch and securely ties the rope. Attach it to the rope or chain you have installed. When you are finished, the swing should be ready to use. If you are making a horizontal swing, start by drilling three pairs of holes in the side of the tire where you have not made a drainage hole. Space the three pairs evenly so that they define three sections of equal size. Space the two holes in each pair to allow for a U-clamp to be inserted. Pass each clamp through the link at one end of the remaining chains before inserting its legs into one of the pairs of holes in the tire. Secure the clamps in place with the accompanying plates and nuts. When you are done, attach the last link of each chain's free end to the swiveling hook. Once the safety hook is locked, the swing should be ready to use. If you are making a vertical swing, simply attach the ends of the rope to the tire opposite the drainage holes you drilled. Make a flat knot and ensure that the rope is tied very tightly. All that’s left is to try it out.

Make sure you fully understand the assignment's requirements and the expected outcomes. With all this information in mind, it will be easier for you to understand what type of research you need to conduct, the question your thesis should answer, and the objectives you should achieve. If you have any doubts about the assignment's requirements, approach your teacher. Meet with them after class when they are free, or send them an email. If you choose to email them, remember to include your name and the class time in the subject line. Once you have chosen a topic, start writing everything you know. During this process, make connections between the ideas you already know and try to ask questions that you may not yet be able to answer. A true brainstorming session is simply writing everything that comes to mind without paying much attention to organization, the time you've spent, or the expected results. However, there are many more structured brainstorming methods you might consider.

Practice freewriting. Freewriting is a technique where you set a timer (usually for 5 to 10 minutes) and write continuously until that time is up. Don't worry about punctuation, grammar, aesthetics, etc. The most important thing is to keep writing. At the end of the exercise, you should find that you know more than you thought. Then, you should start making connections between your ideas. Create a mind map. This technique involves making a kind of map by noting some of your ideas and visually connecting (using colors or drawing lines between connected elements) items that share similar characteristics. This will help you visualize more clearly the ideas that are related to each other. Start with preliminary research. Remember to choose reliable and reputable sources and focus on areas you are already familiar with. The most reliable research sources are scholarly articles and books found in libraries and academic databases such as World Cat or Google Scholar. Choose websites that end in .gov or .edu, which will be more reliable than .com or .org sites. Avoid sources like Wikipedia, personal blogs, and non-academic sites in general. A great way to determine if a source is reliable is to check the author's credentials. If the author has a PhD in a related field, then they are an expert. On the other hand, if the author is a blogger or journalist, they may have less stringent fact-checking requirements. Some non-academic sites may contain reliable information or point to other reliable sources. They can also be useful for getting basic information on a topic. Even if you suspect that you suffer from obsessive-compulsive disorder, never try to self-diagnose. Psychiatric diagnoses can be quite complicated and are meant to be made by a mental health professional to treat patients. If you find yourself unable to manage obsession and compulsion problems on your own, consider consulting a psychologist or mental health professional for diagnosis and treatment. Ask your doctor for a referral if you don’t know where to start. Psychotherapy for treating this disorder involves discussing your obsessions, anxieties, and compulsions during regularly scheduled sessions. Although psychotherapy cannot cure the illness you suffer from, it can be effective in managing OCD symptoms and making them less noticeable. Therapy can help treat this disorder in 10% of cases, but it can improve symptoms in 50 to 80% of patients. Therapists and psychologists use different techniques during their sessions to help their patients overcome this disorder. Some therapists use exposure therapy, where patients are gradually exposed to anxiety-provoking external situations, like deliberately choosing not to wash their hands after touching a doorknob. The therapist collaborates with the patient until that anxiety begins to decrease. Some therapists use imaginary exposure, which involves a short narrative intended to simulate situations that often provoke anxiety in the patient. The goal of this imaginary exposure is to teach the subject to control their anxiety arising from a situation and to desensitize them to anxiety triggers. There are also several medications that have proven effective in the short-term treatment of obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors associated with OCD. Keep in mind that such medications treat symptoms without actually curing the disorder. Therefore, it is preferable to combine medication treatment with therapy sessions rather than using just one of these treatments. Among these medications are:
- Clomipramine (Anafranil)
- Fluvoxamine (Luvox CR)
- Fluoxetine (Prozac)
- Paroxetine (Paxil, Pexeva)
- Sertraline (Zoloft)
Although many people see this condition as a problem caused solely by a dysfunction of the individual's brain, it is important to remember that the onset of OCD is often preceded by a series of stressful or even traumatic events. Being in situations like the death of a partner, losing an important job, or being diagnosed with a terminal illness can cause stress and anxiety in the individual. In some people, this stress and anxiety may gradually push them to control certain aspects of their life that may seem less important to others. Work to establish a strong support system, where your past experiences will be respected appropriately. Surround yourself with people who will show support for you. Feeling supported by a group has proven to be important for improving mental health in general. Find ways to spend more time with people you care about. If you do not feel sufficiently supported by all these people you are in contact with, consider going to a local support group for people suffering from OCD. These meetings are generally free and can be an excellent way to start talking about your disorder with others who are both supportive and somewhat familiar with what you are experiencing.

### Instruction2:
Do not self-diagnose OCD; consult a mental health professional if needed. Psychotherapy can help manage symptoms, and various techniques like exposure therapy are used. Medications may also help but should be combined with therapy. Build a support system with understanding people and consider joining a local OCD support group for additional help.

What is a solar eclipse? It occurs when the Sun, Earth, and Moon are perfectly aligned. The Moon is positioned between the Sun and the Earth, causing the revered god Ra of the Egyptians to vanish from our view. There are four types of solar eclipses: Total eclipse: the Sun is completely obscured. Annular eclipse: when the size of the Moon is smaller than that of the Sun. Hybrid eclipse: an intermediate between the two previous types. Partial eclipse: the Moon only obscures part of the Sun. A solar eclipse can last from a few seconds to several minutes, with a total eclipse lasting up to about 8 minutes. The solar disk is replaced by its silhouette, and most of the solar corona becomes visible. This phenomenon is possible because the distance between the Sun and Earth is 390 times greater than the distance between the Earth and the Moon. The diameter of the Sun is 400 times larger than that of the Moon, making the ratios approximately the same (~0.5 degrees (~30') of angular arc). If you, your children, or friends want to admire a beautiful solar eclipse, there are certain things you should NEVER do, as it would put your health in serious danger. Do not observe a solar eclipse with a telescope or binoculars. Do not look directly at it, even with polarized sunglasses or protective film. The Sun's rays are powerful and can quickly damage your eyes. Even if you think your fancy Ray-Ban sunglasses provide total protection, that is not true in many cases, especially when looking directly at the Sun. Infrared and ultraviolet waves are invisible but can significantly harm your eyesight. To safely watch the eclipse, you can create a pinhole projector using a needle (or punch) and a piece of paper or cardboard and another sheet. The image will pass through a small hole and be projected onto the paper or the ground a few meters away. You will then see the image of the Sun appear as a crescent obscured by the Moon. You will need to find the right balance between the size of the hole and the projection distance, which may require several tries. Take a piece of cardboard and pierce a hole in the center with a pin or needle. Now place a second sheet on the ground; it will serve as a screen for when the show starts. Stand upright and turn your back to the god Ra. Hold the perforated cardboard above the ground next to your body or just above your shoulder. Make sure your head doesn’t block the view. The cardboard you hold must be placed between the Sun and the sheet on the ground. When your pinhole projector is perfectly positioned, you will distinctly see a circle on the sheet of paper on the ground. The edges of this circle may appear a bit blurry, which is normal. To fix this, simply move the pierced cardboard closer to or further from the ground (toward the screen sheet). Once the Sun is obscured by the Moon, the point you see on the ground will transform into a kind of zero (0) for a total eclipse or a small crescent for a partial eclipse. To watch a solar eclipse comfortably, you can also use a modified camera. To observe the eclipse without projecting its image onto a surface, you can use a telescope, spotting scope, or binoculars, but you must place a solar filter to protect your eyes. Amateur and professional astronomers use them when they want to look at the Sun. They serve two purposes: filter out ultraviolet and infrared rays and reduce light intensity. Solar filters have a fine layer of chrome, aluminum, or silver on their surface. They have a large diameter but are generally quite expensive. If your budget is limited, you can make a Mylar filter. Mylar is a thin aluminized metal sheet and is highly effective. It reduces light intensity by a factor of 1,000,000 while perfectly filtering UV and infrared radiation. You must use perfectly flat sheets that are not wrinkled. Since they are easy to cut, you can easily adapt them for viewing the phenomenon. Cut them and attach two pieces to a pair of glasses! You cannot use Mylar filters on observational instruments, and you must respect the usage deadline. NEVER look at the Sun without protection, and be cautious at the beginning and end of the eclipse if you remove the protection during a total eclipse. You can also protect your eyes with a maximum index glass plate for welding masks or several layers of completely opaque black and white negatives that have been fully developed and contain a silver emulsion. Be careful, as some negative films do not contain this, such as color films. If you have a telescope, spotting scope, or binoculars, you can safely enjoy the show by projecting the image captured by your instrument onto a screen, wall, or the ground. Without a filter, you must NEVER look at the eclipse through the instrument (it would permanently damage your eyes) but simply project its image somewhere. Start by covering one side of your scope (preferably the side you would normally look through) or binoculars with their protective cap or a piece of cardboard. Turn your back to the Sun and hold or position your observational instrument so that the uncovered side points toward the god Ra. Align your binoculars, telescope, or spotting scope using its shadow. Position the instrument about 30 centimeters from the surface onto which you will project the image. This can be a large sheet of white paper on the ground or attached to a wall, a screen, a white wall, or a white sheet held with one hand. The further the surface receiving the image is from your instrument, the larger the projected image of the Sun will be. Practice well before the eclipse so you are ready when the show starts! To ensure the projected image is perfectly stable and you are free to move, place the observational instrument on a table, chair, or tripod. You can use this method to observe the Sun even when there is no eclipse. You should place the instrument in the shade after about a minute of observation to avoid damaging it, as it will heat up quickly. Let it rest for several minutes before trying again. You can look at the Sun directly while protecting your lovely eyes with a maximum index glass plate used for welding masks. This way, your eyes should be fully protected (even on the sides) throughout the show. This system also works when using a spotting scope, telescope, or binoculars. If the plate can only cover one side of your binoculars, cover the other side with the plastic cap or thick cardboard. If you live in (or near) a big city, there is likely at least one specialized store for astronomical observation instruments! You will find all kinds of filters suitable for different devices like binoculars, spotting scopes, or telescopes. Their prices generally range from 25 euros to 600 euros, depending on your instrument. By purchasing a solar filter from a specialized store, you can be assured that the filter is effective and that your eyes will be well protected from ultraviolet and infrared rays. You obviously need to buy a filter that is perfectly suited to the type of instrument you are using, but if you go to a reputable store, it should not be a problem, as the seller will assist you. If there is an amateur astronomer club in your area, contact them online or by phone, and don’t hesitate to meet with members who will share their knowledge and advice, as they are enthusiasts. If there is an observatory, check what public open days are available and go there. Make sure the filter you wish to use is not damaged. Mylar, for example, is fragile and ineffective when the sheet has been bent or if it is punctured. The filter you use must be securely attached. If it moves slightly, you should ensure it won't fall by securing it with tape. NEVER use filters that must be mounted on the inner end (the side you look through) of an observational instrument. They can be easily damaged by the rays of the Sun concentrated by the lenses or mirrors, putting your eyesight at risk. Only use filters that mount on the outer end (the side opposite to the one you look through).
