Think about what you want and why you want it. Is it an object or an adventure? Once you've determined this, ask yourself a series of questions to prepare for the discussion. Here are some questions to consider: Why do I need this thing? Why should my parents give it to me? If you can't come up with good answers to these questions, it's probably not the right time to approach your parents. If you don't know why you want something, it's unlikely that you'll be able to get it.

To discover what might constitute a "good" reason for your parents to give you what you want, try to understand what they value. Depending on cultural and family differences, this could vary widely. Helping out with the family business or taking care of your siblings may impress some parents, while others might be more impressed by your efforts in school and extracurricular activities. Remember times when they praised you and appreciated your actions; these are the "good" reasons you might have for wanting something.

It is also possible that some parents are swayed by logical arguments. Prepare a few good arguments to justify why you want this object, trip, or adventure. This will demonstrate that you are not acting impulsively and that you have thought things through before presenting your request. You might argue that it will help you progress in school, prepare you for adult life, or support your growth. You can also mention that it will fuel your imagination, provide relief from life's difficulties, or be useful for the whole family or community. Self-centered or irrational desires will be unconvincing. Avoid saying you want something just because your friend has it; for parents, that suggests you are just following others and don't truly value the gift you want. Phrases like "I just want this," "I deserve it," or "I have to have it" are poor arguments you shouldn't use. Additionally, telling them they are bad parents if they do not fulfill your request will likely be ineffective.

Check eBay, Amazon, and other online marketplaces for the lowest prices. If it's a trip, look for the cheapest options and affordable accommodations. When you approach your parents with all this information, they will see that you care not only about what you want but also about their financial resources. Determine how long it will take to save half or even all of the amount needed. If your parents are willing to cover part of it, they will let you know during the discussion. If you almost know you won't get what you are asking for, try to accept that possibility. If you get what you want, you will be more satisfied, but if your fears are confirmed, it will prevent you from resenting your parents.

If your parents refuse your request, it might be because they believe you don't deserve it. Face this directly by offering to work in exchange for what you desire. They will likely respect your effort and dedication. Even if they do not agree with your proposal, maintain your offer to do extra work. This may impress them over time, and you might eventually get what you asked for. You need to prove that you are becoming a responsible person. For example, you can offer to do laundry, clean the kitchen and bathrooms, sweep the floors, care for pets, mow the lawn, pressure wash outdoor surfaces, and tidy up anywhere there is a mess.

Your parents might not have enough money to provide what you want. They might even have the money but feel uneasy about spending it on something perceived as too expensive. Offering to contribute will show them that you are committed and willing to fight for what you want. Look for a part-time job to earn money. If you're not old enough to work, ask them if you can do small jobs for them. Save any money you earn until you can pay for half of what you want (or the fuel for a trip). Only approach your parents when you have everything together. Showing them that you can plan, work, and save on your own may convince them.

Offer to work for what you want and demonstrate responsibility. Research prices and save money to show you care about their finances, and only approach them when you're ready.

Here are the main categories of people who are particularly vulnerable in high heat conditions: the elderly, children, pregnant women, people who work outdoors, those who have just moved to a warmer climate than their original area, people with health problems such as those suffering from asthma, high blood pressure, diabetes, lung disease, or obesity, individuals particularly prone to dehydration such as those with digestive disorders, and those taking medications that increase sensitivity to heat, such as certain diuretics, antihistamines, beta-blockers, tranquilizers, and antipsychotics. This will give you enough time to prepare for a period of intense heat. Be aware that on days when the air is very humid, your body sweats more slowly, making it harder for it to cool down naturally. Also note that it can take only a few minutes of exposure to extreme heat for thermal shock to occur, but it can also happen gradually after prolonged exposure to heat over several days.

This is more important than creating a quality control department. Depending on the size of your business, you may already have one. This department tracks and documents quality issues and works to resolve them. However, relying on such a department can lower your company's performance, as it may lead other employees to think that quality is not their responsibility. Investing in training for all your employees at all levels, rather than in a single department dedicated to quality control, will show your employees that they are also responsible for improving the quality of your services, regardless of their role in the company. Look for gaps in your employees' training. Have your employees attended seminars on customer service, online or in-person, to improve their performance? Organize training sessions targeting the gaps your team is experiencing, such as customer service at the checkout or how to address a consumer in a meeting. For instance, if you want to improve checkout service, organize a training session on this topic. You can show them how to greet customers, process transactions quickly and efficiently, and handle cash or card transactions. You can also set up role-playing scenarios, with one employee acting as a cashier and another as a potential customer. Don’t stop training after the first few days or weeks of your employees' work. Teach them to always seek improvement and learn more about their work, their company, and the best ways to serve your customers. This program will teach new employees the importance of quality and service in your business before they start working. It should be a well-structured program presenting the products, services, and also the strategy of your company. It should reinforce its approach to customers and your commitment to quality customer service. The program should also include a presentation of your service approach. Provide examples of past and current customer service issues and the solutions you have implemented to address them. This will help your new recruits understand your approach to the system and how you solve problems. Encourage cooperation between your old and new employees. More experienced workers can share their experience and advice to help improve their performance in certain positions or roles. Your former employees can also give them tips on providing quality service to your customers. When possible, personally conduct the orientation of your new employees. Lead one of the training sessions to show them that you are seriously committed to this program. This will also give you the opportunity to instill your company’s values in them before they take their positions and set them on the path to success. A simple rule states that employees should greet customers within their first 30 steps or 30 seconds in your store. This attention will ensure that your customers feel welcomed and wanted, giving them a better impression of your business. Ensure your employees are trained to communicate this welcome with their body language as well as their words. A “Hello” will not have the same impact if your employee does not make eye contact with their customers, does not smile, or does not stand upright. If your business is fully digitized, set up an automated response system so that your customers know their message has been received and that you are acting to resolve their issue. This means you need to show them that what they do daily in their workplace has a huge impact on customer satisfaction. Linking individual employee behavior to a broader system will help instill the importance of quality service on a daily basis. One way to do this is to challenge your employees to commit to providing the best possible service to your customers for a whole month. At the end of this month, show them proof of improvement in sales performance and a decrease in customer complaints. Encourage your employees to view customer service as a story of your business. Your employees are the main representation with which your customers will know your business. Generally, their behavior helps create the culture of your company or store. By understanding that these interactions with customers are not limited to just the checkout interaction but are primarily about how customers feel in-store, you can more easily motivate your employees to improve the quality of your service. For example, the Trader Joe's chain of stores in the United States is regularly ranked as one of the best companies in terms of customer service because its employees are trained to recreate a relaxed atmosphere in-store and offer personalized recommendations on their products. This approach makes the in-store experience more enjoyable, encouraging customers to return even though their stock may be more limited than other stores. Goals should represent a challenge while remaining achievable. Research has shown that having specific and challenging goals leads to better performance. Avoid overly simple or vague goals like “Do your best.” Focus on specific actions and attitudes, such as greeting all customers with a smile, assisting them in the fitting room, and ensuring that the checkout transaction is quick and pleasant. For example, the team of a Las Vegas casino had to meet the goals set for each position within the company, as well as those established for the group in the area. The manager worked with each employee to ensure that the goals were challenging but attainable. The company used a combination of goals and rewards to motivate each team member. Motivate your employees by recognizing their accomplishments and their ability to meet or even exceed customer service goals. There are two main ways to reward your employees. Financial rewards: one of the simplest ways to implement financial rewards is to increase your employees' salaries and bonuses. But if you are not in a position to give your employees more money at once, you can enhance their finances in other ways. For example, grant them the time off they request, offer better social security, and be flexible with childcare or eldercare. Non-financial rewards: create a reward program that shows your employees how much you appreciate their work and attention to customer service. Focus on a program that recognizes their length of service, positive feedback from customers, and employee accomplishments. Use rewards such as plaques, certificates, products from your company, gift cards, or giveaways. Although these rewards are not monetary, they will give your employees a sense of pride and accomplishment, which is necessary to keep them motivated. Another way to motivate your employees and empower them in their position is to give them the opportunity to advance within your company. Create management positions for the more senior employees or those who demonstrate a high level of performance. Encourage new recruits to aspire to a higher position and give them the opportunity to prove their skills. You may decide to hold an annual performance meeting so that your employees can assess themselves and know how to improve their performance for the coming year. These meetings are also a great way to encourage positive employee behaviors and show them the direction their career is taking in your company. It is crucial that you show your employees that they can be as helpful as they are friendly. A polite and pleasant salesperson who knows nothing about the goods they are selling will not satisfy your customers. Likewise, an employee who knows about an issue but cannot resolve it will not impress your consumers. If your employee cannot provide an immediate solution, train them to establish an action plan to resolve the issue as quickly as possible. For example, if a customer reports a problem with one of your lawnmowers, but your store is about to close in 5 minutes, you could promise them that you'll send a salesperson to their home the following morning to repair their model. This is how you will establish extremely high-quality customer service. Every customer who enters your store or business should leave happy. Even if you or a member of your team makes a mistake, the customer should leave satisfied. Do not act defensively or accuse your customer of making a mistake. Listen patiently and offer your sincerest apologies. Then, explain how you plan to resolve their problem. The politest employee in the world will not make excuses for their incompetence or inability to meet a customer’s needs. For example, let's say a customer returns to the store with a blouse that has been damaged in the washing machine and they have kept the receipt from two days ago. Start by apologizing to the consumer for the poor quality of your inventory. Then explain that although you cannot refund them (as indicated on their receipt), you can offer them a gift card to your store equal to the amount of the defective item, as well as a discount on their next purchase. This way, your customer will recognize that you have addressed their request and want them to be satisfied with your services. You can also assure them that you will investigate with your manufacturer and remove the remaining stock from your shelves. Customers who are dissatisfied with your services should be encouraged to return to your store. This will allow you to satisfy them, much more than simply contributing to solving their problem. Listening to their feedback will also show them that you care about what they have to say and that you take their opinion seriously. Conduct a quality survey at least once a year. Maintain an open dialogue with your employees by starting each day with a motivational speech before the doors of your store open. Present the expectations for service quality for every customer who enters your establishment. Present specific behaviors that will show customers that your team wants to provide them with quality service, such as greeting them as soon as they step through the door, engaging them at checkout, and offering assistance in selecting their size or trying on items in the fitting room. Encourage open communication and regular feedback to continually improve customer service quality.

Most birds make noise, either by singing or squawking. Their voices are most often heard in the morning and before dusk. Some birds are noisier than others, but you should know before bringing one home that you cannot prevent them from making noise. Cockatoos are considered one of the bird species that use vocal communication the most. Their voices are usually heard only in the morning and evening, but they are universally recognized as the loudest birds. Macaws are also very noisy, but their calls are typically heard in the morning and evening, similar to cockatoos. Conures emit high-pitched, piercing sounds but only make noise to "call" their owner, not to "chat." Cockatiels, budgerigars, lovebirds, and parakeets make noise throughout the day. If you're looking for a quiet bird, avoid these species. Whenever you respond to your bird's incessant squawking, regardless of the species, it will think that this annoying behavior helps attract your attention. Bird owners often react to squawking by showing affection or even running into the room and yelling for the bird to be quiet. Ignoring these noises will be difficult at first, but that is the only way to get the bird used to not seeking attention this way. Leave the room when your bird starts making noise and only return when it has stopped squawking or screaming. Only return if the bird has been quiet for at least 10 seconds. Praise your bird and reward it with a treat when it is quiet. It will understand that it only gains your affection by being quiet. Praise your bird when it whistles or murmurs, especially when it is not screaming. This method is particularly effective with parrots, as it is easier to teach them words at a low volume than sounds. Do not raise your voice if your bird screams or sings loudly. Speak softly whenever you address your bird or are in its presence. Always praise your bird immediately when it lowers its volume to mimic yours. If your bird begins to make acceptable volume sounds, give it food or a toy every time it behaves this way. Over time, it will associate this vocal range with what you choose to reward it with. Make sure to praise it immediately; if there is a delay between its action and your reaction, it will not make the connection. Whenever your bird screams or talks loudly, stop showing it affection and leave the room immediately. Use a specific treat as a reward. Try to find out what your bird enjoys most and use its favorite treats for training sessions. Your companion will be more inclined to comply with your requests.

Consistency in training will help the bird associate quiet behavior with positive reinforcement.

Take half an hour to prepare your body and mind for studying to be more effective. Go for a short walk before studying. Stretching your muscles with a little walk will help your body relax and clear your mind before you start revising. If you're hungry, eat something before studying, but opt for a light snack or small meal. Eating too much beforehand might make you feel tired and hinder your concentration. Your mindset when starting work can affect your efficiency. Work on maintaining a positive mindset every time you begin studying. Think positively whenever you study. Remember that you are acquiring new skills and abilities. Don't get discouraged if you find something difficult. Remember that you study to improve, so it's normal not to understand everything. Avoid catastrophic thinking or black-and-white thinking. Catastrophic thinking includes thoughts like: "If I don't understand now, I will never understand." Black-and-white thinking sounds like: "I never pass my tests." Instead, try to be realistic. Think: "I'm struggling with this information for now, but if I persist, I'm sure to understand it." Don't compare yourself to others. Focus on achieving a good outcome for yourself. The success or failure of others shouldn't matter. Mnemonic devices are ways to remember information by creating associations. This can be extremely helpful when you want to study smart. Many people remember topics by stringing words together to create phrases and giving those words a meaning that relates to the information they need to remember. For example, the phrase: "I love to teach a useful number to the wise! Immortal Archimedes, artist, engineer, who can appreciate your judgment?" helps remember the first thirty decimals of π by counting the number of letters in each word (i.e., 3.14159265358979323846264338379). Make sure to use mnemonic methods that you can easily recall. If you create one, choose words or phrases with personal significance that you can easily remember later. If you took notes, rewrite them. By rewriting your notes and slightly changing the words, you will engage more with the material. You're not just repeating the information; you're trying to re-explain it to yourself. This can help you process the information and remember it more easily later. Don't just copy the information. Try to condense it to its simplest point. Then, try to condense it further until you get to the essential points.

To study effectively, take time to prepare your body and mind. Go for a walk and eat a light snack if hungry. Maintain a positive mindset and avoid catastrophic or black-and-white thinking. To help your rabbit feel comfortable and safe with you, make sure they do not perceive you as a giant. Lower yourself to your rabbit’s level. You could sit, squat, or lie on the floor. Allow your rabbit the opportunity to come onto your lap or physically interact with you. Some rabbits enjoy cuddling and will readily sit on your lap. However, most rabbits prefer to remain independent during playtime. Rabbits can be fearful, especially at first. Do not force your rabbit to play certain games or with specific toys if they do not seem interested. Let the rabbit explore at their own pace. Do not roughhouse with a rabbit like you would with a cat or dog, as they are naturally skittish and you might frighten them. Cheerfully greet your rabbit before opening their cage, saying their name and a positive phrase like “hello.” This way, the rabbit will associate you with a joyful feeling and will be more inclined to interact with you. You will need: a French press, freshly ground coffee beans suitable for espresso, a spoon for dosing, a stick for stirring, and 50 cl of hot water. Remove the lid and the mesh filter connected by a metal rod. The filter and piston will press the ground coffee into the hot water. Make sure its edges are raised when you remove it. Use a kettle or pot on the stove. When the water begins to heat, pour a little into the French press to warm it, preventing the glass from breaking due to sudden temperature changes when you pour in boiling water. The grind size is crucial for an espresso-like drink. If you purchase pre-ground coffee, look for espresso blends. If grinding your own, choose beans labeled for espresso. There isn't a strict type for this drink, but professional roasters often use specific beans for espresso to achieve the desired flavor and texture, as they are roasted to enhance the espresso's taste. To grind your coffee, use a grinder with an espresso function. Burr grinders crush the beans between two burrs, producing a uniform powder, while blade grinders chop the beans, which can lead to an uneven grind. A very fine grind is necessary for espresso, finer than regular coffee for a French press or percolator. The fine powder enhances flavor and integrates better with the hot water under pressure, but it shouldn't be so fine that it passes through the filter. The issue with a French press is that the holes in the filter are larger than those in an espresso machine. Aim for a sand-like consistency for your ground coffee. You can grind the beans slightly finer than usual for your French press, but not too fine unless you're okay with some sediment in your cup. Pour about 35 g of ground coffee into the container. This step is delicate, as the goal is to make an espresso. When prepared in a machine designed for it, approximately 16 to 21 g of coffee is needed for 25 cl of water. Since a French press is larger, try doubling the amounts. You'll have leftover coffee, but that's fine. Pour a little nearly boiling water over the coffee, wait a few seconds, then add the rest of the 50 cl of water. The water should not exceed 93 °C; around 90 °C is perfect. Before adding all the water, pour a bit over the coffee grounds to "bloom" and release the flavors. Briefly stir the mixture with a long spoon to avoid clumping and achieve a frothy consistency. Next, place the lid on and push the filter down just to the surface of the liquid. Do not push it all the way down yet; let the coffee steep until the water is very dark (about 3 to 4 minutes). The longer you steep the coffee, the stronger it will be, but don't steep too long hoping for stronger espresso flavor. It may take some experimentation to find the right steeping time. Remember that this time controls the extraction: if too short, the coffee will taste sour; if too long, it will be bitter. Hold the lid in place and slowly and steadily push the piston down until it stops. You can experiment by pushing the piston halfway, pulling it back, and then pushing it down fully to create a fine foam layer. Let it rest briefly before serving. If you want to catch very fine grounds, pour the coffee through a coffee filter or a clean cloth. If using a paper filter, it may slightly alter the taste and texture, as it will retain some foam that contributes to the espresso's texture and could make the coffee taste slightly oily as it passes through.

### Instruction2:
To make espresso with a French press, gather the necessary items: a French press, freshly ground espresso beans, a spoon, a stirring stick, and hot water. Warm the French press with hot water, then add coffee grounds (around 35 g). Pour nearly boiling water over the grounds, stir briefly, and let steep for 3 to 4 minutes. Slowly push the piston down to separate the grounds, let it rest, and then serve, optionally filtering to catch fine grounds.

It is clear that accidents or spills can happen, but if you have spilled water or any other type of liquid on your engineered hardwood floor, you need to clean it up promptly. If you leave the liquid sitting on the material for a long time, it could seep inside and damage the plywood or the hardwood itself. It could also leave a permanent stain. When cleaning up spills on the floor, you should gently blot to wipe them up. Avoid scrubbing or applying strong pressure to clean the area. If you do, you risk warping the hardwood plywood or pushing the liquid into the wood and damaging it. Although these abrasive liquids will clean some surfaces, there is still a high chance they will damage your engineered hardwood floor. Vinegar and ammonia could erode or damage the surface of the plywood beneath the top layer of hardwood. You should refrain from using a steam cleaner on engineered hardwood floors. Although a steam cleaner can be a useful tool for cleaning carpet, it is not recommended for engineered hardwood at all. In fact, steam may damage the surface of the wood by forcing water to seep into the top layer and into the plywood. A steam cleaner can potentially cause more damage than other cleaning techniques that use excess water (like a very wet mop). Since a steam cleaner forces moisture to penetrate the wood, it could damage the lower layers of the fiberboard or plywood. It is highly discouraged to use abrasive and harsh cleaning products (like a metal brush or steel wool) on hardwood floors. There is a strong chance these products will cause scratches or otherwise damage the plywood beneath the hardwood. Although engineered hardwood floors are more resistant to liquids than standard models, you still should not leave water or any liquid cleaner on your material. Dry the floor by patting it with a towel if any excess liquid cleaner remains after you have finished cleaning. Similarly, if you use a damp mop, you risk damaging the top layer of the hardwood. If the wood absorbs a significant amount of water, it could warp. Therefore, you need to ensure all water is removed after cleaning the floor.

### Instruction2:

If you live in a place where winters are milder, in hardiness zones 7, 8, or higher, you should be able to plant poinsettias in your garden, and they will grow year after year. If you live in a location where temperatures drop below freezing in winter, it is better to keep them in a pot and care for them indoors. Poinsettias are native to Mexico, and they need a warm climate to thrive. If you bought a poinsettia plant to decorate your home during winter, keep it in a pot until spring, even if winters are relatively mild. The poinsettia should remain in its pot until temperatures are warm enough for transplanting. Water it occasionally until spring. At the beginning of spring, in March or April, cut the poinsettia back to about 25 cm. This will encourage it to start a new growth cycle and prepare for replanting. Water and fertilize it once a month until early summer when it’s time to replant. Choose a spot where it will receive morning sunlight and some light during the heat of the afternoon. Rake and aerate the soil to a depth of 30 to 40 cm. Enrich the soil by incorporating organic compost if necessary. Poinsettias prefer rich, well-drained soils. Dig a hole as wide as the pot it is in and plant the poinsettia in it. Gently pack the soil around the base of the stem. Lay mulch around the stem 5 to 7 cm thick to help keep the soil cool and moist. Spread 12-12-12 or 20-20-20 fertilizer at the beginning of the growing season or use compost if you prefer. If your soil isn’t very rich, you may need to fertilize once a month. Water the plant at the base when the soil around the stem feels dry to the touch. Avoid overwatering, as this can cause fungus to attack the plant’s leaves. Occasionally pinch off small leaf shoots to encourage the plant to flower. You can discard these shoots or use them to make cuttings. Cut old shoots in late fall or early spring to encourage the growth of new branches the following spring. Cut 20 cm long shoots from the tender tips of poinsettia stems, or take 45 cm of woody branch from the plant to obtain a new poinsettia. Dip the end of each shoot or branch in rooting hormone, then plant it in a pot filled with potting soil or a vermiculite-based mix. Keep the potting soil moist but not too wet for several weeks until roots develop. Add fresh mulch around the base of the plant to keep the soil warm during winter. The poinsettia can spend the winter outside in areas where the soil temperature does not drop below 7 degrees Celsius. Dig up the plant and bring it indoors if you live in a region with cold winters where the soil temperature drops below 7 degrees Celsius.
